rationale: Jul 8-9 OPCW Executive Council approved the first destruction plan, for Category 3 (unfilled) chemical weapons at the Al Qutayfah destruction facility, along with storage agreements for Al Qutayfah and Homs. The May finds were 54 Latamneh-type aerial bombs and 25 Ghouta-type rockets, so bombs are the likeliest type. Al Qutayfah is a former Scud base, so missile warheads are possible.

Max Whitlock withdrew on Jul 13 with a hand injury. England is now fielding a second-string squad (Whitehouse, Tobin, Nathan, Yolshin-Cash) without Jarman, Fraser or Hepworth, which narrows the gap to Canada (Dolci, Emard). England is still the favourite for the Jul 24 team final.

Jun 27-28: Malaysia's National Security Council chief said the government is negotiating with Myanmar to take back Rohingya (120-130k registered), and Home Minister Saifuddin was tasked with concrete arrangements. Myanmar is open to 300k returns from Bangladesh. Thailand's camp-closure plan (KTNews, Jun 2) is about self-reliance, not returns.

Soft June CPI (Jul 14) killed July hike odds: Polymarket has a hold at 96% (Jul 20). Logan said on Jul 16 that modestly higher rates are warranted, and TD (Jul 20) says Hammack effectively signalled a dissent for a hike. Continuum expects no more than two hawkish dissents, with Kashkari less likely.

Six candidates, including new entrant Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett (Guyana). A General Assembly debate is set for Jul 23, with the first straw poll reported for Jul 23 (EastAfrican) or late July (The Clinic). Lowy (Jun 24) calls Grossi the longtime leading candidate and Washington's favourite. Grynspan is well liked but her Council support is uncertain, and Bachelet faces US and China scepticism.

Jul 16-21: the Danube at Baziaș is at about 1,650-1,750 m3/s, the lowest in 30 years and comparable to 2003, when Cernavoda Unit 1 was shut. Romania has restricted irrigation and is releasing water from Olt and Argeș reservoirs to protect Cernavoda cooling. Both units are still at full power, with flows forecast at about 1,750 until Jul 27.

Pathirage is in form, having added an Ostrava win (86.57) to his Rome 92.62 and Doha 88.68, and Hindustan Times (Jul 21) calls him the favourite. Nadeem confirmed on Jul 13 that he will defend his title but has no 2026 marks. Neeraj's season best is still 85.69. Qualification standings are noisy, so the spread is kept.

Pathirage (92.62 world lead, wins in Rome, Doha and Ostrava) is the clear favourite for the Jul 31 final per Hindustan Times (Jul 21). Neeraj and Nadeem are both entered, with Nadeem confirmed Jul 13 but without a 2026 competition yet. Peters has a 86.38 season best and Walcott is the 2025 world champion.

Heyman (Jul 15) names the Cubs, Braves and Rays as the strongest bidders, with the Dodgers a wild card and the Astros interested. Nightengale lists the Dodgers, Yankees, Blue Jays and Padres as finalists. The Tigers have surged to 46-52 (Jul 18, 3.5 games out of a wild card), so a trade is less likely, but this is conditional on one happening.

As of Jul 21 the field includes world No. 3 Cameron Young (solo 2nd at the Open on Jul 19), No. 7 Gotterup (three 2026 wins), No. 5 Henley, No. 11 Burns (Open 54-hole leader), Schauffele, Spaun, Clark, Si Woo Kim and Koepka. No Scheffler or McIlroy.

Jul 20 entry list seeds: Auger-Aliassime, de Minaur (defending champion), Shelton (wildcard, world No. 5), Medvedev, Fritz, Musetti, Tien, Tiafoe. Fritz's chronic knee tendonitis flared at Wimbledon on Jul 8. Alcaraz is returning at Cincinnati, not DC.

Jul 20-21: Kostyuk, Jovic, Paolini, Muchova (surgery) and Mboko have withdrawn. Pegula (wildcard, two-time DC champion) is the top seed, followed by Svitolina, Osaka (beat Sabalenka at Wimbledon), Shnaider, Kalinskaya, Keys, Fernandez (defending champion) and Navarro.

Jul 1: Iran's foreign ministry said demining under the MoU will be done by Iran alone, while France and Oman agreed to demine jointly with partners. The war resumed mid-July, with Iran striking Omani sites. Iran-Oman talks on the strait continue at technical and political levels (Jul 11), so Oman remains the most plausible partner if any deal comes.

Trial sessions on Jul 8-9 (Al-Ahram) heard a forensic expert say 2018-19 health ministry decrees list analogues, which weakens the defence's scheduling argument. Prosecutors demanded death on Jun 11. No referral to the Mufti and no verdict date reported yet. Under Art. 33 the penalty is death, reducible to life.

Two searches and the local archive found no reporting on a transfer of Shehadeh's diaries. The forecast remains a prior: Oxford's Middle East Centre Archive, Birzeit, AUB (his alma mater) and Columbia (Said papers).

Heavy fighting in late June and early July around Kulbus in West Darfur between the Joint Force (including Minnawi's) and the RSF, with RSF reinforcements from El Geneina, Saraf Omra and Kabkabiya. West Darfur RSF commander Abdel Rahman Juma Barkallah was sentenced to death in absentia on Jul 12. Abu Lulu is reportedly fighting in Kordofan. Highly uncertain.

Hamilton campaign internal poll (Jul 13-16, n=600 likely Democratic primary voters, Sunflower State Journal Jul 21): Hamilton 30, Christy Davis 13, Noah Taylor 10, Schmidt 5, Murray 2. This is consistent with the June Change Research lead. Hamilton also has a large money advantage.

The 2nd Test is at Queen's Park Oval, Aug 2-6, in the rainy season, so draws are likely. West Indies just beat Sri Lanka 1-0 (Jul 7), their first series win in three years. Pakistan's reset squad under Babar (named Jul 5) has no Shaheen or Naseem and several uncapped players.

McMorrow suspended her campaign on Jul 5. Polls disagree: Glengariff (Jul 8-11) Stevens 48-41, Tavern (Jul 6-7) Stevens 42-41, Data for Progress for a pro-El-Sayed PAC (Jul 10-14) El-Sayed 54-41. Kalshi and Polymarket had El-Sayed in the mid-60s (Jul 16). Peters endorsed Stevens and AIPAC has spent about $30M for her; Sanders, AOC and Warren back El-Sayed.
